title: UN Security Council — Middle East briefing and consultations under resolution 2334, on the general debate's closing day
source: EST: onu.diplomatie.gouv.fr/en/french-presidency-security-council-program-work, fetched direct 2026-09-15 (HTTP 200, browser headers) during the unga-81-general-debate-2026-09-22 D-7 pulse-check adjacency sweep. France holds the September 2026 Council presidency; the page is titled 'Provisional Agenda of Work of the Security Council - September 2026 as of 31 August 2026', published 2 September 2026, and its transcription reads verbatim 'Monday, 28 September Briefing (A.M.). Middle East [2334]. Consultations (A.M.). Middle East [2334]. OPCW report due.' Filed estimate/EST: on three counts: the document is the presidency's PROVISIONAL programme rather than an adopted one (securitycouncilreport.org's September-2026 Iran forecast, read by the unsc-iran-panel-mandate-vote-2026-09-17 lane on 2026-09-10, records that China and Russia blocked adoption of the programme in both March and June), CONFIRMED_PREFIX in scripts/event-scan-validation.mjs carries no UN or diplomatic slot, and the event-research lane may not self-confirm an event it discovered in-sweep. Checked 2026-09-15
notes: PROPOSED AS THE DATE ANCHOR THAT CORRECTS A LEG OF THE PROPOSER'S OWN RESEARCH, NOT AS A CATALYST. The unga-81-general-debate-2026-09-22 initial research (2026-09-04) concluded from press.un.org's 09-01 write-up that NO dated Iran or Middle East Council meeting fell inside high-level week. France's own published provisional programme refutes that on the Middle East file: this 09-28 briefing and consultations land on the general debate's closing day, alongside an unnamed 'Briefing (11:00 A.M.) TBC' on 09-23 and an informal interactive dialogue with the League of Arab States on 09-24. It remains SUPPORTED on the Iran file, which carries no meeting inside 09-22 to 09-28 at all. WHY low AND symbols: [] ARE THE HONEST FILING, and why this one was proposed while the other three were not: resolution 2334 (2016) is the standing quarterly briefing on Israeli settlements in the occupied Palestinian territory - a named, recurring, calendared item with an identifiable subject, which is what makes it filable at all - but it has no Hormuz, no sanctions-enforcement and no crude channel, and the proposer's ledger measures the general-debate window itself as BELOW an ordinary week for SPY (0.29% day-one / 0.72% five-session median absolute move against a 0.49% / 1.19% baseline, n=11 debates 2015-2025). The 09-23 'TBC' slot was deliberately NOT proposed: a dated slot with no named subject is a watch item, not a calendar entry, and the proposer's ledger registers it as such. NOTE THE SEAM THIS SWEEP ALSO FOUND AND DID NOT TOUCH: the same French programme dates 'Sunday, 27 September Res. 1929 experts mandate expires', a second primary (after securitycouncilreport.org) against the 26 September carried by the tracked unsc-iran-panel-mandate-expiry-2026-09-26 and by main.un.org. That file is sibling-owned and the discrepancy is recorded in the proposer's ledger row rather than amended from here (one file per owner, issue #1449). Estimate widens caution only; it licenses no date-keyed action.
